checks.claim: C1: Actual objects are the original d1 objects (covariance with amplitude, separable nonnegative test, positive compact family, whole-line F with both constants, massless physical wave generator), not a surrogate
checks.reason: target-v1 l.14-28: psi=f(t)q(x) with f,q nonzero, nonnegative, compactly supported smooth, f supported in (0,1); k(t)=int_0^1|t-s|^-a f(s)ds; V_b=b(Gamma*q), K=[b0,b1] containing range k([0,1]), 0<b0. This matches joint-gaussian-tilt (5): h(t,x)=int_0^1|t-s|^-a(Gamma*psi(s,.))(x)ds=k(t)(Gamma*q)(x). k(t)>0 on [0,1] because the kernel is positive and f>=0, f nonzero; k is continuous because a<1, so a positive b0 exists. Gamma is 'the original nonzero d1 Riesz/white covariance including its amplitude' (l.22), consistent with tilt Sec.1 (c_Gamma retained). F (l.9-10) matches local-flow Sec.4 (closure of compact smooth phases plus (1,0),(0,1) in E_uloc). The generator (v,w)->(w,v''+V_b v) is the massless wave with potential +V_b, matching the sign of the tilted retained potential (tilt l.268). l.28 excludes a circle operator; l.55 makes the L2 theorem only an input. V_b satisfies the local-flow (5.6) admissibility (tilt (6), constant part 0), so P_b is an accepted deterministic flow on F on every finite horizon. Concatenation gives all t>=0. One wording issue is in minor findings.

checks.reason: p448 image (A1): H=H_0+V, H_0=-(1/2)Delta. Then H_b/2=-(1/2)d^2-V_b/2, so V_Simon=-V_b/2 and E=-lambda_b^2/2. The crosswalk (l.11-16) is exact, and no factor sqrt2 arises.

So V_Simon=-V_b/2 has negative part V_b/2 and positive part 0. The integral is <=2*(1/2)||V_b||_inf=||V_b||_inf, as the kato screen (l.8-15) says, and sup_K||V_b||_inf=b1||Gamma*q||_inf (tilt Sec.3). checks.claim: C2c: Teschl second edition identity and Theorem 10.2 hypotheses (bounded, vanishing-at-infinity class) correctly applied
checks.reason: The title image shows 'SECOND EDITION', GSM Volume 157. The p258 image shows Theorem 10.2: V real, V in L^inf_inf + L^2 for n<=3. Its conclusions are relative compactness, H self-adjoint on H^2, bounded below, sigma_ess=[0,inf), and C_c^inf a core. Teschl's H_0=-Delta, as in the same page's hydrogen example (10.5), so the kinetic normalization matches H_b with no rescaling. The p201 image shows the tail of the class description, 'bounded Borel functions which vanish at infinity', and its use in (7.45). V=-b(Gamma*q) is bounded, continuous and tends to 0 (Riesz tail ~|x|^-alpha; white case compact). The crosswalk claim is correct; the partial visibility of the definition is noted in minor findings.

checks.claim: C3a: Projection algebra exact — e_b=(p_b,lambda_b p_b), ell_b=(<p_b,v>+<p_b,w>/lambda_b)/2, Pi_b^2=Pi_b, P_b(t)Pi_b=e^{lambda_b t}Pi_b, decaying partner in kernel, ell_b(e0)>0
checks.reason: If H_b p=-lambda^2 p, then on span{p} the generator acts as alpha'=beta, beta'=lambda^2 alpha. The functional (alpha+beta/lambda)/2 evolves at rate lambda. ell_b(e_b)=(1+1)/2=1 when ||p_b||_2=1, so Pi_b^2=Pi_b. The partner (p,-lambda p) gives ell_b=(1-1)/2=0, so it lies in the complement as l.53 states. ell_b(e0)=(1/2) int p_b>0 for strictly positive integrable p_b. The constant entries need p_b in L1 together with weighted local-Sobolev summability, which l.40-41 correctly leaves as obligations. Left invariance ell_b o P_b(t)=e^{lambda t} ell_b is not listed, but it follows from the target bound: apply the semigroup property and let t->infinity. So it is not a missing hypothesis.

checks.claim: C3b: The S1 statement is sound and non-vacuous for the actual positive profiles, including Riesz profiles with infinitely many bound states
checks.reason: Existence: in d1, any nonzero, nonnegative, bounded, vanishing V_b gives a negative bottom (dilated-trial variational test; for Riesz tails the potential term even dominates the 1/L kinetic term). With Teschl 10.2/10.13 the bottom is then simple, positive and isolated. Riesz tails ~|x|^-alpha with alpha<1 produce infinitely many negative eigenvalues accumulating at 0. The target explicitly allows this (l.52) and removes only the top wave mode. The feasible eta is limited by min(lambda_b-mu_{2,b}, lambda_b), and this gap is positive. H_b=-d^2-bV_1 is norm-resolvent continuous in b, so on compact K the gaps and inf lambda_b are uniformly positive and an eta>0 independent of b exists. eta<inf lambda_b is necessary because the continuous spectrum at threshold 0 gives non-decaying, even linearly growing, F orbits (e.g. constant (0,1) data). I found no counterexample. Heuristically, the F transfer for compact data, far translates, and constants cut off at radius O(t) is consistent with an exp((lambda-eta)t) bound up to polynomial factors. This is a plausibility check, not a proof.

checks.claim: C4: The analytic obligation boundary is honest; no conclusion is assumed or hidden in a named input
checks.reason: Existence and isolation are 'Establish' obligations (l.32). Uniform constants are required (l.34). Pairings on F 'MUST be defined and bounded ... by decay/local Sobolev duality' (l.40-41). 'No premise may assume the desired F-complement estimate' (l.43). l.55-59 separates the L2 spectral theorem from the H^{1/2}xH^{-1/2} spectral calculus and from the F transfer. It names the growing global Sobolev norm of localized data and the removed-projection tails after exponential growth, and it states that compact phases are not dense in F. A polynomial prefactor is allowed only as an intermediate with an exact uniform conversion (l.49-51). The source-crosswalk transfer mechanism is labeled UNPROVED and 'not a lemma or a substitute for S1'. The named inputs (local flow, tilt) supply no spectral or complement content.

checks.reason: The tilt retains the potential g zeta_r W^delta + zeta_r h(delta u,x) with h=k(t)(Gamma*q). On fast block m the frozen operator is H_{k(m delta)} with b in K, matching the family. l.69-72 correctly separate the masked Riesz profile zeta_r V_b from V_b: ||(1-zeta_r)V_b||_{W1inf}=O(r^-alpha)->0, which needs its own fixed-block estimate, while white compact support gives equality once the mask is 1. l.61-67 lists slow-b changes, random block errors (accepted (7.3) only bounds per-block differences), initial entrance, the whole product, the final fractional block and the positive terminal displacement average as S2. The rate 2Lambda(h)-v/2 is consistent with tilt (13), where s=1/sqrt(delta) gives cost v/(2 delta) against squared growth exp(2Lambda/delta). l.75-76 asserts no rate. minor: target-v1 l.23 wording defect: 'Do not set Gamma*q=q outside the white case' implicitly suggests Gamma*q=q in the white case. In the accepted tilt (Sec.1/3), white Gamma=c_Gamma delta_0, so Gamma*q=c_Gamma q. The binding definition V_b=b(Gamma*q) 'including its amplitude' (l.22) controls, but the guard should read 'Gamma*q=c_Gamma q only in the white case' to avoid dropping the amplitude.
